headline: NC school districts receive $311 million in grants as facility needs climb to $18 billion
summary: Seven NC school districts awarded $311M in state grants for school construction and renovation. Statewide facility needs jump 37% to $18B over five years.

headline: Commentary: Missouri voters rejected more than an abortion ban
summary: Missourians voted to protect reproductive freedom and transgender rights, rejecting attempts to restrict these freedoms in successive elections (2024 and 2022). In 2022, 55% voted against reinstating an abortion ban, a wider margin than the 2024 vote (51.6%). Anti-trans policies were not widely embraced, with voters prioritizing cost of living and affordability over political distractions. Missourians' repeated rejection of freedom restrictions signals a need for policymakers to respect personal freedoms and engage in meaningful dialogue.

headline: WA slated to get another $177M in rural health funding
summary: Washington's Olympic Area Agency on Aging offers free dementia screenings for rural residents, funded by federal rural healthcare improvement grants. The state is set to receive $177M in 2027, ranking ninth lowest among states, with $159 per rural resident. Funding aims to reshape rural healthcare, including workforce growth, tribal health, technology, behavioral health, and hospital infrastructure. Public health benefits include early dementia detection and improved rural healthcare access.

headline: Brown students take to the streets to help Rhode Islanders navigate Medicaid changes
summary: In Rhode Island, Brown University public health students are educating residents about Medicaid changes, including new restrictions and work requirements. They are canvassing neighborhoods and partnering with local organizations to distribute information in nine languages. The initiative aims to clarify complex changes and support those impacted.

headline: Will some Florida cities challenge Uthmeier and kill their immigration enforcement agreements?
summary: Florida cities and towns are debating whether to end cooperation agreements with ICE known as 287(g) programs, with Tallahassee's mayor ready to defy threats from the Attorney General. The Attorney General maintains that local governments must comply with federal immigration laws, while the incoming governor vows to keep Florida from becoming a "sanctuary state."

headline: After state employees didn’t get raises in 2026, Idaho state legislator pay frozen for 1 year
summary: Idaho legislators' pay will remain frozen at $25,000 in 2027 before increasing by about 6.7% in 2028. The Citizens Committee on Legislative Compensation, not legislators, sets pay. State employees have not received raises since 2025 due to budget cuts during the 2026 session. Next year's legislature plans to increase state employee pay.

headline: Lawmakers call for promise of campaign neutrality if the tax is raised to fund IWiLL
summary: Iowa lawmakers discuss funding for Iowa Water and Land Legacy trust, with concerns about raising sales tax due to potential campaign repercussions. The sales tax increase could reach a penny, with discussions on how to allocate the additional revenue.

headline: Vermont grapples with measles as US loses elimination status
summary: In Vermont, measles cases were confirmed in Orleans County, prompting state and local health officials to contain the outbreak. The state has high vaccination rates overall, but affected areas have lower rates. To combat the outbreak, the state is offering measles vaccines and providing prophylactic antibody infusions for vulnerable individuals. The Vermont Health Department recommends vaccinating children against measles, mumps, and rubella once they are over 1 year old, and encourages parents in affected areas to consult their pediatricians for early vaccination if their children are between 6 and 12 months old.

headline: New Mexico education department proposed rules draw backlash from lawmakers, school officials
summary: On Nov. 18, 2026, the New Mexico Public Education Department (PED) faced criticism from lawmakers and school officials for proposing close to 30 rule changes, many with tight public comment deadlines, affecting various aspects of K-12 education. Critics argue the volume and timing of proposals pose significant challenges, with some changes potentially impacting Native American students and educators. The PED was urged to postpone or withdraw these rules until after Gov.-elect Deb Haaland's inauguration and the legislative session.

headline: SC superintendent hopes to make performance-based teacher bonuses permanent
summary: In South Carolina, a pilot program rewarding teachers based on student test score improvements has awarded $5.5 million to over 750 teachers across 97 schools. The state superintendent plans to make this program permanent, with an annual budget request for the 2027-2028 school year. The average award was $8,000, with Darlington School District having the highest participation rate and average award amount. The program aims to recognize excellence and encourage teachers to stay in the classroom, with the state also raising minimum teacher salaries. Critics argue for a more equitable approach that includes all teachers, such as those without standardized tests to measure student progress.

headline: Photojournalists sue St. Paul Police over use of force during ICE raid
summary: St. Paul police used chemical munitions against protesters and journalists during an ICE immigration raid, violating constitutional rights and leading three photojournalists to sue the police department.

headline: Huffines’ limit on data tax will cost Texas $18 billion, comptroller’s office projects
summary: Don Huffines, now serving as interim Texas Comptroller, was previously a Republican candidate for the role during the 2026 State Republican Convention in Houston.

headline: Western Arkansas hospital joining initiative to expand access to doulas
summary: UAMS expands doula program to Mena Regional Health System, aiming to improve maternal healthcare access in rural Arkansas. This initiative aligns with public health goals, as Arkansas has high maternal and infant mortality rates, with residents calling for increased investment in these areas. The state has yet to extend postpartum Medicaid coverage, with legislation failing in 2023 and 2025.

headline: Indiana won’t implement Medicaid work requirement grace period
summary: The Indiana Family and Social Services Administration has decided not to participate in a federal six-month grace period for enforcing Medicaid work requirements due to state law constraints, potentially impacting the state's Medicaid budget and compliance efforts starting January 1, 2022.

headline: GAO prods ICE for new immigration detention plans
summary: The Government Accountability Office urged ICE to plan immigration detention costs more effectively, following a $2.8 billion budget increase for FY2025. ICE's previous attempt to convert warehouses into detention centers resulted in millions of dollars in waste, and the agency has yet to propose a new plan for the funds.

headline: New bird flu cases appear in dairy herds as state ag, vet officials seek vaccine urgency
summary: Bird flu, typically seen in poultry, has begun infecting dairy cows in 22 states, with at least 146 cases in 2025 alone. States urge the USDA to prioritize vaccine approval for cows, warning of the virus' potential to become endemic. The risk to humans is low but dairy workers are at higher risk, with three deaths reported nationwide.

headline: Task force dives into possible changes to Kansas school funding as current formula is set to expire
summary: The Kansas Legislature's Education Funding Task Force is reviewing potential new school funding models to replace the current formula, which expires in 2027. Changes could affect funding for individual districts, with some potentially gaining or losing money. The current formula faces challenges, including inflation adjustments not keeping pace with actual personnel cost increases.

headline: Federal judge in Colorado holds ICE officials in contempt over ‘re-detention’ policy
summary: A federal judge in Colorado held ICE officials in contempt for immediately re-arresting immigrants upon court-ordered release, but declined sanctions after ICE ceased the policy. This incident highlights tensions between ICE and federal courts over immigration enforcement, potentially impacting future policy and compliance.

headline: Becerra podría enfrentar déficit presupuestario de 2 mil millones de dólares si explota la burbuja de la IA
summary: California's budget faces significant challenges due to its dependence on income from high-value stocks, which may drop due to market fluctuations. The Legislative Analyst's Office predicts a $2 billion deficit by 2028, which could increase to $15 billion without cuts or tax increases. The state may not have sufficient reserves to cover larger deficits if the market crashes. Governor-elect Xavier Becerra will inherit a more dire financial situation than initially projected, with potential cuts to health services for immigrants.

headline: People Still Sick 5 Years After Fuel Leak Into Oʻahu Water
summary: Five years after a fuel leak contaminated drinking water at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, some residents continue to experience serious health issues, including tremors, rashes, and gastrointestinal problems. A registry tracking symptoms has found patterns similar to long COVID or chronic fatigue syndrome. While the Navy focuses on decommissioning the fuel facility, affected families seek better healthcare coverage and further investigation into past spills.
